Subject: RFI: security controls + evidence for Redwood inference

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this—our team is compiling vendor evidence for the platform review. Two asks up front: can you send your most recent SOC 2 Type II report (redacted is fine), ISO 27001 cert, and a completed SIG questionnaire export? In addition, we need brief clarifications on a few control points so we can map to our internal requirements:

- Do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK) for Private deployments? If so, which KMS/HSM integrations are supported and is key escrow allowed?
- Where are audit logs retained for Private vs Hosted — rolling retention policy and whether logs are immutable for at least 12 months?
- Does your Hosted environment support regionally isolated storage for EU data obligations?

If you can get the packet to us by EOD Thursday that would keep us on schedule for procurement. Feel free to drop a short crosswalk CSV mapping SIG control IDs to Redwood controls — that accelerates our review.

Cheers,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Senior Vendor Risk Analyst
Harvest Bank

Hi Liam / Dana,

Thanks — we appreciate the clear list. Attached is an initial package: a redacted SOC 2 Type II (covering 2026 period), a scan of our ISO 27001 certificate, and an exported SIG workbook ("SIG_responses_v1.xlsx") with our control statements. I included a short one-page mapping called "SIG quick map" in the workbook to get you started.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- CMK / Private: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via integrations with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem HSMs using KMIP. Key escrow is customer-configurable but not required; we can provide a tech note.
- Audit logs: Private retains raw audit events in the customer's VPC for the configured retention (default 13 months); Hosted retains logs in our secure observability store with tenant separation (default 13 months). Immutable WORM-style retention is available as an add-on — we can scope depending on your retention SLA.
- Regional isolation: Hosted has region-level data controls; customers can request EU-only tenancy for data storage and processing for a managed onboarding.

Next steps:
1) Attachments below.
2) I will route your request for a SIG control-to-evidence CSV to our compliance team and loop in Karthik for the KMS/HSM tech note.
3) If helpful, we can do a 30-min walk-through tomorrow afternoon. Let me know a window.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Liam / team,

Thanks for the patience — please find the updated items below and a short summary to address your audit questions. Larger packet linked in Drive for secure download.

Attachments (included): SOC2_TypeII_redacted_2026.pdf, SIG_responses_v1.xlsx (SIG crosswalk tab + CSV export included).
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890 (for procurement reference)

Short answers:
- CMK / custody model: In Redwood Private, keys are customer-controlled by default when configured for CMK mode. We also offer an optional managed-custodian service for customers that prefer Redwood to handle key lifecycle under an SLA (requires a contract addendum). Supported integrations: AWS KMS (customer keys or grants), Azure Key Vault, and KMIP-compatible HSMs. Rotation: customers can define rotation cadence; we support scheduled rotation and manual rotation; export of plaintext keys is not permitted (keys can be wrapped/exported only via approved HSM channels).
- Audit logs / immutability & retention: For Private, audit events are written to the tenant's storage target; events are signed (HMAC) and timestamped by our logging pipeline. Default retention is 13 months; we can extend to 24 months or more on request and enable WORM retention for immutable archives. Hosted follows the same retention controls; WORM is available as an add-on.
- SIG crosswalk: attached CSV tab maps SIG IDs to Redwood control IDs and points to evidence file names and the Drive link for each artifact. Controls that rely on 3rd-party attestations are flagged in the rationale column.

Open items / next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the redaction level on the SOC2 PDF is acceptable for Legal. If additional redactions are required, Marissa can produce a further-trimmed version.
2) If you want a technical walkthrough, I can set a 30-min call — I have availability Mon/Tue 10–12 PT next week.
3) If you require a managed-custodian addendum for keys, I can route to our commercial team and include pricing.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through any of the mappings.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
